public_rationale: Earlier newsletter warnings about automated misinformation and web pollution are documented. Independent evidence shows low-quality AI educational videos and an AI-enabled misinformation campaign reaching millions of views. The claim that all three named harms are happening remains unsettled. Internet-crime complaints increased, but those totals do not isolate AI-enabled scams. A vendor's identity-fraud rate also fell relative to 2024 while remaining above 2023. These findings neither establish nor refute the asserted increase in cyberscams. The assessment does not require an invented web-quality index or substitute rising losses for more scams.
limitations: The ordinary reading of enshittification remains qualitative.
The educational-video study covers a narrow sample and found limited prevalence.
Social-media views can include repeat views.
Complaint counts depend on reporting behavior and are not direct incidence estimates.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: The harms Marcus warned about years ago (enshittification of the web, mass misinformation, more cyberscams) are now all happening.

statement.excerpt: In this newsletter years ago, I warned about the enshittification of the web, the mass spread of misinformation, increases in cyberscams, and so on, and it’s all happening.
statement.document_title: A few dark words about chatbots and death

from_speaker: In this newsletter years ago, I warned
our_interpretation: Assess the three named harms. The unspecified phrase 'and so on' adds no separately testable commitment.

Read 'enshittification of the web' as deterioration through the proliferation of low-quality or misleading AI-generated content. This does not require a particular web-quality index or deterioration of every website.
Read 'mass spread of misinformation' as false information reaching large audiences, rather than merely being generated in experiments.
Read 'increases in cyberscams' as more scam activity or victimization. Higher monetary losses alone do not establish an increase in occurrence.
The surrounding discussion connects these harms to generative AI. Evidence should establish its involvement, without requiring proof that AI is the sole cause.
Use 2025, the latest completed calendar year before publication, for the ongoing conditions. Earlier newsletter posts establish the provenance of the warnings only.
criteria.support_condition: Earlier newsletter records establish the named warnings, and independent evidence documents web pollution by low-quality AI content, large-audience dissemination of AI-enabled misinformation, and an increase in cyberscam activity involving AI during the target period.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reliable, appropriately scoped evidence establishes that a named warning was misrepresented or that a named harm did not occur as asserted. Failure to locate evidence, successful mitigation in one setting, or a decline in a narrow fraud measure is insufficient by itself.

evidence.excerpt: accelerate the enshittification of the internet
evidence.explanation: Establishes an earlier newsletter warning about automated misinformation and web pollution. It supplies provenance, not independent evidence of the harms.

evidence.publisher: JMIR Medical Education; institutional copy at Corewell Health
evidence.explanation: The February–March 2025 sample documents low-quality AI content in educational video results. The authors also describe it as not especially prevalent in this sample, so this supports occurrence rather than web-wide deterioration.

NewsGuard identifies AI-enabled false narratives targeting France and measures their cumulative dissemination through March 2025. This supports mass dissemination; views are not unique viewers or proof of belief.

evidence.locator: Key findings, overall identity fraud rate
evidence.explanation: This cautions against treating increased sophistication as increased incidence. The vendor's identity-fraud rate fell from 2024 but remained above 2023; neither comparison alone settles the broader cyberscam claim.

evidence.locator: Second paragraph of the press release
evidence.explanation: Total internet-crime complaints increased, but that category is broader than scams. The release separately identifies AI-related complaints without a comparable earlier AI series, so it does not establish increasing AI-enabled scam incidence.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Locate the earlier cyberscam warning and obtain comparable observations showing whether AI-enabled scam activity or victimization increased against the relevant earlier baseline. Broader evidence of web pollution would strengthen assessment of that component.
